title: On September 6th, India's Supreme Court decided that equal citizenship isn't conditional.
caption:
On September 6th, India's Supreme Court decided that equal citizenship isn't conditional.

A dancer, a journalist, a chef, a business executive and a hotelier - five petitioners took a colonial-era law to India's highest court. On September 6, 2018, the Supreme Court unanimously struck down Section 377 as it applied to consenting adults.

Delhi High Court first struck the law down in 2009. The Supreme Court reversed that in 2013, sending it back to Parliament. It took five more years and five more petitioners to settle it for good.

Equal citizenship under the law is as much a part of India's growth story as any factory or export number. The next 20 years are being built by people who can now build them as full, equal citizens.
